quarterly_data.signal: Arista's 10-Q: Arista outsources most manufacturing to contract manufacturers, and a significant portion of its purchase orders for finished goods and strategic components, including integrated circuits consigned to contract manufacturers, consists of non-cancellable commitments. As of June 30, 2026 it had $9.7 billion of non-cancellable purchase commitments not recorded on its balance sheet, of which $9.4 billion had expected receipt dates within 12 months and $0.3 billion beyond 12 months, plus deposits with its contract manufacturers to secure purchase commitments of $124.4 million versus $53.0 million at December 31, 2025. Arista says it continues to increase purchase commitments to respond to the rapid deployment of AI networks and to navigate tightening supply in the memory and silicon markets, and that constrained memory and silicon availability could prevent it from shipping end-customer orders on time.
quarterly_data.figure: $9.7 billion purchase commitments ($9.4 billion within 12 months, $0.3 billion after) as of June 30, 2026; contract-manufacturer deposits $124.4 million vs $53.0 million
